claims.text: Grants support the growth and development of sculpture across historical, modern and contemporary registers.
Grants support research that expands appreciation of sculpture.
Categories cover exhibitions.
Categories cover commissions.
Categories cover acquisitions.
Categories cover conservation.
Categories cover conferences.
Categories cover publications.
Categories cover long-term research.
Categories cover research and travel grants for individual scholars.
Grants are available to UK and international non-profit organisations.
Grants are available for exhibitions.
Grants are available for exhibition catalogues.
Grants are available for commissions.
Grants are available for conferences.
Grants are available for research.
Grants are available for non-commercial publications.
Grants are available for the development of collections through acquisitions.
Grants are available for the development of collections through conservation.
Grants are available for the development of collections through cataloguing.
Grants are available for the development of collections through display.
Individual sculpture historians, academics and conservators can apply to the Research and Travel category.
Applications are not accepted from individuals who are independently wishing to create, inform, develop or research their own practice.
Residency programmes are not supported.
Central or building costs are not supported.
Traditional memorials/figurative statues are not supported.
Commercial publishing projects are not supported.
Play equipment is not supported.
Community gardens are not supported.
Wellbeing activities are not supported.
Community project applications will only be considered when the applicant is a non-profit arts organisation.
New Projects and Commissions category is for exhibitions, exhibition catalogues and sculpture commissions.
Exhibition or commission projects aiming to encourage new thinking about sculpture or sculpture history are eligible.
Exhibition or commission projects contributing to public awareness and appreciation of sculpture are eligible.
The maximum grant available for New Projects and Commissions is £20,000.
Acquisitions and Collections category is for acquiring new sculptural works for collections.
Acquisitions and Collections category is for conserving sculpture in existing collections.
Grants for cataloguing and display costs are considered under Acquisitions and Collections.
The maximum grant available for Acquisitions and Collections is £20,000.
Conferences, Lectures and Publications category is to publish a new book or journal.
Conferences, Lectures and Publications category is to stage a conference or other event related to sculpture.
Exhibition catalogues are only eligible under the New Projects and Commissions category.
The maximum grant awarded for Conferences, Lectures and Publications is £5,000.
Long-Term Research grants support extended research projects requiring funding for more than one year.
Long-Term Research grants can be used for a permanent collection catalogue.
The maximum grant available for Long-Term Research grants is £20,000.
Research and Travel grants are available to sculpture historians, academics and conservators.
Research and Travel grants support research and publishing on sculpture conservation, production, history and/or interpretation.
Research and Travel grants support research costs.
Research and Travel grants support travel.
Research and Travel grants support photography.
Research and Travel grants support archival access.
Applications for Research and Travel grants cannot be for informing or developing an artist’s own work, and/or professional practice.
The maximum grant available for Research and Travel grants is £2,500.
Grant applications are administered using Flexi-Grant.
Applicants need to register to create an account to submit, manage and review grant applications.
FAQ guidance is available for help on the application process and answers to common questions.
Applications are considered four times per year.
Autumn applications close on 1 September at 23:00.
Projects starting or opening to the public no sooner than 1 January 2027 are eligible for the Autumn round.
Winter applications open on 1 November at 9:00.
Winter applications close on 1 December at 23:00.
Projects starting or opening to the public no sooner than 1 April 2027 are eligible for the Winter round.
Spring applications open on 1 February 2027 at 9:00.
Spring applications close on 1 March 2027 at 23:00.
Projects starting or opening to the public no sooner than 1 July 2027 are eligible for the Spring round.
Summer applications open on 1 May 2027 at 9:00.
Summer applications close on 1 June 2027 at 23:00.
Projects starting or opening to the public no sooner than 1 October 2027 are eligible for the Summer round.
Organisations must be registered to apply.
Registration requests must be received one week before the deadline.
Registration requests received after the deadline will be registered for the following round.
A video introduction is available to guide through the application process.
FAQs and further information are available.
Downloadable documents including grant terms & conditions and logo versions are available.
The Henry Moore Institute in Leeds supports researchers through its sculpture research programme.
Research fellowships allow researchers to spend a month using facilities in Leeds.
Research fellowships include accommodation.
Research fellowships include travel.
Research fellowships include subsistence expenses.
The Artist Award Scheme offers financial support to artists during times of crisis.
The Artist Award Scheme was launched in 2020.
The Artist Award Scheme was a response to the Covid-19 pandemic.
The Artist Award Scheme has run three times.
In 2020, the Foundation awarded £60,000 to 40 artists through the Artist Award Scheme.
In 2022, the fund for the Artist Award Scheme was expanded to £100,000.
In 2025, the fund for the Artist Award Scheme was expanded to £100,000.
The Artist Award Scheme fund was expanded in response to the escalating cost-of-living crisis in the UK.
The Artist Award Scheme cannot be applied for.
Recipients of the Artist Award Scheme are selected through a UK-wide nomination process.
The nomination process for the Artist Award Scheme involves leading voices from the non-profit arts sector.
The category and criteria information should answer most application and eligibility queries.
Additional support is available in the grants application portal.
Eligibility can be assessed in the grants application portal without submitting an application.
Further grants support or help with the application portal can be requested by completing a form.
For all other queries, refer to the Contact us page.
The organisation cannot advise whether a project will be funded, only if it is eligible.
